pages.text: The Celestial Distributor is a zero-buffer capability proxy. It starts from all adjacent blocks by default. A compatible wrench selects all sides or one of six directions with the same interaction and face arrows as an ME Pattern Provider. Every hop of directional discovery follows that direction in a straight line and may traverse another distributor on the line, which consumes one of the default 32 target slots without becoming a resource target. Changing direction immediately abandons the old bound path.

Incoming resources are divided as evenly as possible among accepting targets. A redstone signal switches to sequential insertion, filling targets in cursor order; removing the signal restores balanced insertion. Jade shows the current mode when installed.

Node maintenance values have mode-specific meaning. Balanced insertion maintains each accepting device independently and treats an item matching position as that device's local slot. Redstone sequential insertion maintains all devices in aggregate and treats the position as a device index. The same distinction applies to fluids, chemicals, FE, Mana, Source, and supported Souls.

Extraction views all targets as one endpoint and does not enforce equal shares. The distributor has no hidden inventory. Only Sky Logistics simple pipes and logistics nodes recognize it; vanilla hoppers and third-party pipes do not connect.
Craft it with Prismarine in the four corners, Lapis Lazuli on all four sides, and a Redstone Comparator in the center. No altar, Eulogia Crystal, or Celestial Stone is required.

Performance: discovery caches the physical slots exposed on the access side. Each extraction cursor position maps directly to one physical slot, so a hit costs one probe. Simulation builds a transfer plan that execution reuses; after budget exhaustion the line resumes from its cursor next tick.

Each access face caches targets independently. An unchanged rescan preserves routes, heat, and balanced cursors; a changed rescan migrates surviving machine state by block position and access face. An unfinished index delays only that distributor resource by indexingRetryTicks (20 ticks by default), without recording a transfer failure or rebuilding other lines.

Hold a Celestial Configurator and aim at the distributor to outline every target in its current cache in cyan. The client requests a snapshot only when the aimed distributor changes or once per second while aiming; it never triggers BFS every frame.
